summary.purpose: Derive and update the status of insurance policies based on effective, expiry and current dates while preserving existing cancelled statuses, and write the updated policy records and any validation errors to output files.
summary.high_level_narrative: The program starts by obtaining the system current date and validating it. It opens three sequential files: POLICY-IN (input master policy records), POLICY-OUT (output updated records) and ERROR-OUT (error log). It then reads each input record in a loop. For each record it validates the effective and expiry dates, checks that expiry is not earlier than effective, and logs specific error records (S001, S002, S003) when validation fails. If dates are valid, the program copies the input record to the output layout, determines the new policy status using the rule: preserve 'CN', otherwise if current date < effective date set 'PN', else if current date <= expiry date set 'AC', else set 'EX'. When the status changes, the update date is set to the current date and a change counter is incremented. The updated record is written to POLICY-OUT. After all records are processed, the program closes all files, displays processing counters (read, written, changed, pending, active, expired, cancelled, rejected, I/O errors) and returns an appropriate return code.
inputs: POLICY-IN sequential file (fields: PI-POLICY-NO, PI-CUSTOMER-ID, PI-AGENT-ID, PI-PRODUCT-TYPE, PI-POLICY-STATUS, PI-EFFECTIVE-DATE, PI-EXPIRY-DATE, PI-WRITTEN-PREMIUM, PI-CREATE-DT, PI-UPDATE-DT)
outputs: POLICY-OUT sequential file (fields: PO-POLICY-NO, PO-CUSTOMER-ID, PO-AGENT-ID, PO-PRODUCT-TYPE, PO-POLICY-STATUS, PO-EFFECTIVE-DATE, PO-EXPIRY-DATE, PO-WRITTEN-PREMIUM, PO-CREATE-DT, PO-UPDATE-DT)
ERROR-OUT sequential file (fields: ER-POLICY-NO, ER-CODE, ER-MESSAGE)
RETURN-CODE (0 for success, 12 for fatal error)

Comparison of current date with effective and expiry dates to derive status
Copy of input record to output record with possible status change
Update of PO-UPDATE-DT when status changes
Aggregation of counters for read, written, changed, pending, active, expired, cancelled, rejected, and I/O errors
key_dependencies: POLICY-IN, POLICY-OUT and ERROR-OUT file definitions (SELECT statements)
COBOL intrinsic FUNCTION MOD for leap‑year calculation
Standard COBOL file I/O verbs (OPEN, READ, WRITE, CLOSE)
Task 5 POLLOAD (provides valid policy master data) – mentioned as a logical dependency
business_rules: If existing PI-POLICY-STATUS = 'CN' then retain 'CN' and count as cancelled.
If current date < PI-EFFECTIVE-DATE then set status to 'PN' (pending) and count pending.
If current date <= PI-EXPIRY-DATE then set status to 'AC' (active) and count active.
Otherwise set status to 'EX' (expired) and count expired.
Do not derive cancellation status because no cancellation date is available.
Effective date must be a valid calendar date; otherwise write error record with code S001.
Expiry date must be a valid calendar date; otherwise write error record with code S002.
Expiry date must not be earlier than effective date; otherwise write error record with code S003.
When status changes, PO-UPDATE-DT is set to the current processing date.
All file status codes must be '00' for successful open, read, write, or close; otherwise a fatal error is raised.

knowledge_profile.purpose: Read policy master records, validate dates, determine the correct policy status (CN, PN, AC, EX) based on current system date, preserve cancelled policies, write updated policy records and any validation errors to output files, and report processing statistics.

outputs: Processing counters displayed on the console

key_logic: 1. Obtain the system current date (YYYYMMDD) and store in WS-CURRENT-DATE.
2. Open the three sequential files (input, output, error) and verify file‑status codes.
3. Loop reading each input record until end‑of‑file or a fatal error occurs.
4. For each record, validate the EFFECTIVE‑DATE and EXPIRY‑DATE using VALIDATE-CALENDAR-DATE (numeric check, month range, day range, leap‑year handling).
5. If either date is invalid, write an error record to ERROR‑OUT with a specific error code (S001, S002, S003).
6. If dates are valid, call DETERMINE-STATUS to compute the new policy status:
a. Preserve status 'CN' (cancelled).
b. If current date < EFFECTIVE‑DATE → status 'PN' (pending).
c. Else if current date <= EXPIRY‑DATE → status 'AC' (active).
d. Else → status 'EX' (expired).
e. Increment the appropriate status counter and, if the status changed, set PO-UPDATE-DT to the current date and increment WS-CHANGED.
7. Write the (possibly) updated PO-REC to POLICY‑OUT; on write failure set fatal error.
8. After processing all records, close all files, display counters, and return an appropriate return‑code.
9. Supporting routines:
- VALIDATE-CALENDAR-DATE: checks numeric format, month 1‑12, day within month length, uses SET-MAX-DAY.
- SET-MAX-DAY: determines max day for month, calls CHECK-LEAP-YEAR for February.
- CHECK-LEAP-YEAR: implements Gregorian leap‑year rule (divisible by 400 or divisible by 4 but not by 100).

transformations.description: Extract system current date (YYYYMMDD) from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE and store in WS-CURRENT-DATE.
transformations.expression: WS-CURRENT-DATE = FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE(1:8)

transformations.description: Copy input record fields to output record before status evaluation.
transformations.expression: MOVE PI-REC TO PO-REC

transformations.description: If existing policy status is 'CN' (cancelled), preserve it in the output record and increment cancelled counter.
transformations.expression: IF PI-POLICY-STATUS = 'CN' THEN PO-POLICY-STATUS = 'CN'; ADD 1 TO WS-CANCELLED

transformations.description: If current date < effective date, set status to 'PN' (pending) and increment pending counter.
transformations.expression: IF WS-CURRENT-DATE < PI-EFFECTIVE-DATE THEN PO-POLICY-STATUS = 'PN'; ADD 1 TO WS-PENDING

transformations.description: If current date <= expiry date, set status to 'AC' (active) and increment active counter.
transformations.expression: IF WS-CURRENT-DATE <= PI-EXPIRY-DATE THEN PO-POLICY-STATUS = 'AC'; ADD 1 TO WS-ACTIVE

transformations.description: Otherwise set status to 'EX' (expired) and increment expired counter.
transformations.expression: ELSE PO-POLICY-STATUS = 'EX'; ADD 1 TO WS-EXPIRED

transformations.description: If the derived status differs from the original status, mark record as changed, set PO-UPDATE-DT to current date, and increment changed counter.
transformations.expression: IF PO-POLICY-STATUS NOT = PI-POLICY-STATUS THEN ADD 1 TO WS-CHANGED; MOVE WS-CURRENT-DATE TO PO-UPDATE-DT

transformations.description: Validate that a date string is numeric, month is 1‑12, and day is within the month’s maximum day; set WS-DATE-VALID to 'Y' when valid.
transformations.expression: IF WS-DATE-IN NUMERIC AND WS-YEAR>0 AND 1<=WS-MONTH<=12 AND 1<=WS-DAY<=WS-MAX-DAY THEN WS-DATE-VALID='Y'

transformations.description: Derive year, month, and day components from an 8‑digit date string.
transformations.expression: WS-YEAR = WS-DATE-IN(1:4); WS-MONTH = WS-DATE-IN(5:2); WS-DAY = WS-DATE-IN(7:2)

transformations.description: Determine the maximum day for a month, handling February leap‑year logic.
transformations.expression: EVALUATE WS-MONTH ... WHEN 2 IF WS-LEAP='Y' THEN 29 ELSE 28

transformations.description: Leap‑year rule: year divisible by 400 or divisible by 4 but not by 100.
transformations.expression: IF MOD(WS-YEAR,400)=0 OR (MOD(WS-YEAR,4)=0 AND MOD(WS-YEAR,100)<>0) THEN WS-LEAP='Y' ELSE WS-LEAP='N'

transformations.description: If an input record fails any date validation, write an error record with a specific error code (S001, S002, S003) to ERROR‑OUT.
transformations.expression: WRITE ER-REC WHEN validation fails

transformations.description: Accumulate processing statistics (read, written, changed, pending, active, expired, cancelled, rejected, I/O errors) in WS-COUNTERS.
transformations.expression: ADD 1 TO respective counter at each event

business_rules: Preserve existing policy status 'CN' (cancelled) – never derived, only copied.
If current date < effective date → status = 'PN' (pending).
If current date <= expiry date → status = 'AC' (active).
Otherwise → status = 'EX' (expired).
Effective date must be <= expiry date; otherwise record is rejected with error S003.
All dates must be numeric, month 1‑12, day valid for month (including leap‑year rules).
Leap year: divisible by 400 or divisible by 4 but not by 100.
Any file‑status code other than '00' is treated as a fatal error.
If a write to POLICY‑OUT or ERROR‑OUT fails, set fatal error and abort processing.

SYSTEM FUNCTION MOD (used in leap‑year calculation)
